name: CSA N290.7 (Cyber Security for Nuclear Facilities)
description: Cyber security requirements for nuclear power plants and small reactor facilities, second edition, superseding N290.7-14. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission uses it as compliance verification criteria for cyber security at high-security nuclear facilities. It is built on a defensive computer security architecture: digital assets are identified and assigned to security levels (zones), with communication between zones controlled and inbound-only where required. A trade contractor is reached through the licensee's flow-down — most commonly as controls on portable media, on remote access and maintenance tools, on personnel screening, and on the handling of facility digital-system information. Confirm which requirements a specific nuclear contract actually invokes; licensees flow down selectively.
scope: Nuclear power plants and small reactor facilities in Canada, and by flow-down their suppliers, contractors and maintenance providers

families.name: Cyber Security Programme and Governance
families.description: The programme requirements a licensee will ask a contractor to demonstrate before granting access.

controls.name: Documented Cyber Security Programme
controls.description: A cyber security programme is documented, resourced and assigned to an accountable individual, and is auditable by the licensee.

controls.name: Identification of Critical Digital Assets
controls.description: Digital assets whose compromise could affect safety, security or emergency preparedness functions are identified and inventoried, including contractor-owned devices brought on site.

controls.name: Cyber Security Risk Assessment
controls.description: Threats to identified digital assets are assessed, including supply-chain and insider vectors, with treatment decisions recorded and reviewed.

families.name: Defensive Architecture and Access Control
families.description: The zone model that distinguishes this standard from a general IT security framework.

controls.name: Security Levels and Zone Separation
controls.description: Digital assets are assigned to security levels, and communication between levels is controlled — with data flow from lower to higher security levels prevented or strictly mediated.

controls.name: Control of Portable Media and Mobile Devices
controls.description: Portable media and mobile devices are controlled at facility boundaries: scanned, authorized per use, logged, and prohibited in higher security levels unless dedicated to them.

controls.name: Remote Access and Maintenance Tool Control
controls.description: Remote access to facility systems is prohibited or tightly mediated; maintenance laptops and tools are dedicated, hardened, inspected before connection and accounted for.

controls.name: Protection of Facility Digital-System Information
controls.description: Information describing facility digital systems — network diagrams, configurations, credentials, vulnerability detail — is treated as sensitive, access-restricted, and returned or destroyed at contract end.

families.name: Operational Controls
families.description: Monitoring, change control, incident response, supply chain and personnel.

controls.name: Monitoring and Detection
controls.description: Security-relevant events on in-scope digital assets are logged and monitored, with detection tuned for the operational-technology environment rather than borrowed from corporate IT.

controls.name: Configuration and Change Management
controls.description: Changes to in-scope digital assets are assessed for cyber security effect before implementation, with unauthorized change detectable and baselines maintained.

controls.name: Cyber Security Incident Response and Licensee Notification
controls.description: Cyber incidents affecting or potentially affecting facility systems are reported to the licensee within the contracted timeframe, supporting the licensee's own CNSC reporting obligations.

controls.name: Supply Chain and Third-Party Cyber Security
controls.description: Suppliers and subcontractors touching in-scope systems are assessed and bound to equivalent cyber security requirements, with software and firmware provenance verified.

controls.name: Personnel Screening and Cyber Security Training
controls.description: Personnel with access to in-scope systems are screened to the licensee's requirement and trained on the facility's cyber security rules before access, with records retained.
